claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child (or children) who you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a 17-year-old son named Alex who lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A few more questions:

Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and are you financially supporting him (paying for things like food, clothing, and other expenses)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives at home with me and I support him - I pay for his food, clothes, school supplies, all the usual things a parent does.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Next question:

Do you (or Alex) usually live in the UK? And are you a UK resident, or do you have the right to reside in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A couple more questions:

Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status or the right to reside in the UK (for example, through indefinite leave to remain, pre-settled/settled status, or another immigration status)?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more important question:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you in a shared care arrangement where Alex spends equal time with another person (such as another parent)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 17 years old and studying for his A-levels, which means he qualifies as a "qualifying young person" (children under 20 in approved education or training are covered)

✓ You are responsible for Alex - you live together and you provide financial support for his needs

✓ You both live in the UK and you're a UK citizen

✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. You can make a claim and should receive Child Benefit payments.

**Please note:** If your individual income is over £50,000 per year, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge, though you can still claim the benefit. This is separate from eligibility itself.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
